Coherent functional demographic model (product-ratio, demography)

Source: R/model-coherent-fdm.R
coherent_fdm.Rd

The product-ratio method of Hyndman, Booth and Yasmeen (2013), with the functional data models of the demography package: for a group of strata (for example women and men, or the deprivation quintiles of one sex)

Usage

coherent_fdm(
  order1 = 6,
  order2 = 6,
  common_by = NULL,
  smooth = TRUE,
  smooth_args = list(),
  K = 100,
  drange = c(0, 0.5),
  weighted = TRUE,
  beta = 0.05
)

Arguments

order1, order2

Number of principal components of the product and of the ratios.

common_by

Stratum variable(s) defining groups with their own product.

smooth

Smooth the rates of each stratum and year over age before the decomposition (see hyndman_ullah()).

smooth_args

List of arguments of demography::smooth.demogdata().

K

Number of most recent years used to forecast the ratios.

drange

Range of the fractional differencing parameter of the ARFIMA models of the ratios (c(0, 0.5): stationary).

weighted, beta

Weighted principal components of the product and of the ratios, with geometrically decaying weights beta (1 - beta)^i of the years (Hyndman, Booth and Yasmeen 2013: beta = 0.05). weighted = FALSE gives the unweighted decomposition, the default of demography::coherentfdm().

Value

A model specification.

Details

  • the product, the geometric mean of the strata's rates, is modelled with a functional demographic model (hyndman_ullah()) whose scores are forecast with ARIMA models, so it carries the common trend;

  • the ratio of each stratum to the product is modelled with a functional demographic model whose scores are forecast with stationary ARFIMA models, so the differences between the strata stay bounded and revert towards their recent level.

Forecasts of the strata are products of the two. This is the method of demography::coherentfdm() and forecast() for its result; li_lee() is a related model with a common Lee-Carter factor. The Lee-Carter version product_ratio() is deprecated in its favour.

Draws simulate the product and each ratio (uncertainty of the scores and resampled model errors, as simulate() for functional forecasts in demography) and multiply them; the ratios of each path are rescaled so that they multiply to one, as forecast() in demography does for the point forecasts.

Relation to the paper. As in Hyndman, Booth and Yasmeen (2013, Sections 2.1-2.4): the rates of each stratum are smoothed over age first (weighted penalised regression splines, monotone above age 65, through demography::smooth.demogdata()); the product is the geometric mean of the smoothed rates of the group (their Eq. 3), and every stratum has a ratio model (their Eq. 4; they note that J - 1 ratio models would suffice); the scores of the product are forecast with ARIMA models chosen by the algorithm of Hyndman and Khandakar (2008), those of the ratios with stationary ARFIMA models (orders by the same algorithm, maximum likelihood); there is no jump-off adjustment; order1 = order2 = 6 are the numbers of components of their applications. The principal components are weighted, with weight beta (1 - beta)^i for the year i years before the last and beta = 0.05 as in their applications (Section 2.2 and Discussion); demography::coherentfdm() does not weight them by default (weighted = FALSE). The departures:

  • the fractional differencing parameter of the ratio models lies in drange = c(0, 0.5) (the default of demography); the paper names -0.5 < d < 0.5 as the stationary range;

  • prediction intervals come from simulated paths with resampled model errors; the paper gives analytic variances for the rates (their Eq. 8) and simulates for life expectancy. Predictive draws add Poisson deaths in place of the observational variance of their Eq. 8;

  • the ratios of each simulated path are rescaled to multiply to one, and with a hierarchy (see below) the aggregates get a ratio but do not enter the product. Both are package-specific (reference unknown); demography rescales the point forecasts in the same way, and the paper states the constraint for the observed ratios. Predictive draws (mt_forecast(predictive = TRUE)) add Poisson variation of the deaths given the rates and the exposures, and no other observation noise. If intervals are too narrow on real data, that is a property of the model (see recalibrated(), ensemble(), or overdispersed models such as stanmomo(family = "nb")).

With common_by (for example "sex"), each level of that stratum variable forms its own group with its own product (for example the quintiles of each sex). If the data carry a hierarchy (see mt_aggregate_strata()), the product is computed from the bottom strata; aggregates get their own ratio to it. Every group needs at least two strata (hyndman_ullah() models a single stratum).

References

Hyndman RJ, Booth H, Yasmeen F (2013). Coherent mortality forecasting: the product-ratio method with functional time series models. Demography 50(1): 261-283. doi:10.1007/s13524-012-0145-5

Hyndman RJ, Khandakar Y (2008). Automatic time series forecasting: the forecast package for R. Journal of Statistical Software 27(3): 1-22. doi:10.18637/jss.v027.i03

Examples

if (requireNamespace("demography", quietly = TRUE)) {
  x <- mt_example(deaths = "single", years = 1990:2019)
  fit <- mt_fit(coherent_fdm(order1 = 2, order2 = 1), x)
  fc <- mt_forecast(fit, h = 10, n_draws = 50, seed = 1)
}
